subject: Acorn Health: sudden 429 errors — remediation and follow-up
messages:
From: Acorn Health SRE <sre@acornhealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 08:55:00 -0800
Subject: Service spike: clients seeing 429s from Redwood since 08:45 PT

Hi Diego,

We're seeing a sudden increase in 429 responses coming from Redwood for our prod tenant (acorn-prod) starting ~08:45 PT. Rate of errors peaked around 20% of requests for our ingestion endpoint (/v1/ingest). The rest of our downstream processing is healthy.

Attached is a short screenshot from our dashboard showing the 429 spike and a couple of sample request IDs. Can you confirm whether anything changed on your side? This is impacting processing for a handful of customer workflows.

Sample request IDs: rq_9a7c2, rq_bb12f

Thanks,
Jane Lee
SRE, Acorn Health

Attachment: acorn_429_slam_screenshot.png
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Jane Lee <jane.lee@acornhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Service spike: clients seeing 429s from Redwood since 08:45 PT

Jane — thanks for the heads up and the screenshot. I'm escalating to our infra team (cc'd) for immediate investigation.

Immediate actions I'm asking for:
- Karthik: please confirm whether any rate-limit config or deploys touched tenant routing or global caps in the last 3 hours.
- Marissa: I'll coordinate status to Acorn and any commercial remediation (credits) if service was impacted.

We will follow up with a root-cause and ETA for a fix in the next hour. Apologies for the disruption — we're treating this as high priority.

Regards,
Diego Fernandez
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Jane Lee <jane.lee@acornhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 09:38:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Service spike: clients seeing 429s from Redwood since 08:45 PT

Diego / Jane — quick update from infra: we identified a configuration change deployed at 08:30 PT that unintentionally promoted a route-level rate cap to a tenant-level cap for a small subset of tenants (deploy ID: cfg-deploy-20260212-3). That change enforced a tighter token-per-minute ceiling across all endpoints for the tenant rather than just the UI routes.

Root cause (prelim): a templating bug in our ratecap service where the policy scope variable defaulted to "tenant" when an override key was missing. The change was part of a routing cleanup; the code path passed through covered endpoints without a test asserting scope.

Mitigation applied at 09:25 PT: rolled back the deploy and applied a hotfix to the templating code, plus a temporary relax on the tenant cap for acorn-prod. We are also re-deploying a corrected policy with route-scoped caps only.

Status: 429 error rate for the acorn /v1/ingest endpoint is down from ~20% to <1% in our metrics and your sample IDs (rq_9a7c2, rq_bb12f) are now returning 200. We are continuing to monitor for 1 hour and will push an additional guard to make the templating error throw loudly during staging so this doesn't pass review again.

Attachments: remediation_runbook_20260212.pdf, ratecap_config_diff.patch

Next steps (owners):
- Karthik: root cause fix + unit tests (complete by 2026-02-12 14:00 PT)
- Hannah: add a metrics alert for tenant-wide 429 > 5% in 5m for high-volume tenants (complete by 2026-02-13)
- Diego/Marissa: commercial remediation discussion + confirmation to customer (Marissa owner)

I'll follow up with a short post-incident note once the tests and alerting are in place.

—Karthik
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Again, apologies for the disruption. We'll make sure this is fully documented and that preventive changes are in place.

Best,

Subject: Acorn Health — post-incident note and next steps (SUP-4552)

Jane / Tom — follow-up with the post-incident summary and owners:

Incident timeline (summary):
- 08:30 PT: config deploy cfg-deploy-20260212-3 introduced a templating default that scoped a tighter cap at tenant-level
- 08:45 PT: Acorn sees 429 spike on /v1/ingest (~20%)
- 09:25 PT: rollback + hotfix applied; temporary tenant relax for acorn-prod
- 09:45 PT: error rate down to <1%; continued monitoring

Root cause: templating bug in ratecap service that defaulted to tenant scope when override missing. No prior test covered missing-override path.

Corrective actions and owners:
- Karthik Iyer: code fix + unit tests to validate scope variable (ETA 2026-02-12 14:00 PT) — DONE
- Hannah Schmitt: new alert for tenant-wide 429 >5% in 5m for high-volume tenants (ETA 2026-02-13) — IN PROGRESS
- Platform: add pre-deploy policy lint that fails deploys which would promote route caps to tenant scope without explicit approval (ETA 2026-02-19) — OWNER: infra eng
- CS/Finance: issue one-time usage credit for 08:30-09:30 PT (owner: Marissa) — ETA 2026-02-12 EOD

Attachments included: remediation_runbook_20260212.pdf, ratecap_config_diff.patch, acorn_429_slam_screenshot.png

Related ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-4552
Calendar invite: scheduled for 2026-02-13 13:00 PT (shared privately).

If you'd like a fuller write-up for your compliance/audit record (SOC2) we can produce a short incident pack. Let us know.

Apologies again for the disruption and thanks for the quick coordination.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
